title: Machine learning predicts postoperative complications after NSCLC lung resection
summary: In 231 prospectively collected surgical patients (37 complications, 16%) from the LANTERN consortium, machine learning with feature selection identified pathologic score (AUC 0.72, 95% CI 0.62-0.81) and pre-operative FEV1_TEOR (AUC 0.77, 95% CI 0.67-0.89) as the most relevant variables. In an external surgical series of 232 patients, FEV1_TEOR and the combination held, while the pathologic score alone was weaker. The event count is small, discrimination modest and the algorithms are not named in the abstract; this is a version 1 preprint.
ai_technology: Machine-learning models with feature-selection algorithms on 80 clinical and 43 spirometric variables
organization: Catholic University of the Sacred Heart
